Playbook.name: F5 WAF — Critical Attack Type Passed the WAF (Single Event) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A single, highest-fidelity event: a rating>=4 Command Execution, SQL-Injection, Remote File Include, Server-Side Code Injection, Trojan or Other-Application-Attack that the WAF did NOT block. One such event is enough to warrant investigation. Triage question: did this specific critical request reach and affect the backend?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A single successful command-exec or SQLi against a banking app can compromise the server or database outright.

Assets.AssetType: F5 BIG-IP ASM / Advanced WAF fronting JCB internet banking and public web apps
Published banking applications and their backend servers

LogSources.LogSource: F5 ASM CEF events via syslog -> logs-cef.log-* (observer.vendor F5)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: F5 ASM logging to CEF over syslog, parsed into logs-cef.log-* (verified live).

CEF fields: deviceCustomString4=attack_type, deviceCustomNumber2=violation_rating (>=4 = real attack), deviceCustomString1=security policy, requestUrl, requestMethod, deviceCustomNumber1=HTTP response code, deviceCustomString6=source geo, cef.name=violation name, event.action=passed|alerted|blocked.

Signal.Name: Critical attack passed
Signal.Details: One rating>=4 critical-class attack type with action != blocked.

Input.name: $attack_type
Input.description: The attack type (deviceCustomString4) from the alert.

InitialAssessment.Rule: A single passed critical exploit is treated as an incident until backend integrity is confirmed; do not down-rank because it was 'only one event'.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether this critical exploit reached the backend and whether the source is running a broader campaign.

Step.name: Full context of the critical request(s)
Step.Purpose: Get the exact URL, method, policy, and backend response for the critical passed event.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "F5" AND source.ip == "$source_ip" AND cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2 >= 4 AND event.action != "blocked" AND cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4 IN ("Command Execution","SQL-Injection","Remote File Include","Server Side Code Injection","Trojan/Backdoor/Spyware","Other Application Attacks") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4, cef.extensions.requestMethod, cef.extensions.requestUrl, cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber1, cef.extensions.deviceCustomString1, cef.name, event.action | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: deviceCustomNumber1 (response) 2xx/5xx on a command-exec/SQLi URL is the decisive reached-backend evidence. Read the URL for the payload (e.g. ;cat /etc/passwd, UNION SELECT). action=passed is worse than alerted.

Step.name: Is this source running a broader attack
Step.Purpose: A critical single event from a source already flagged for sustained/multi-app activity is part of a live intrusion.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "F5" AND source.ip == "$source_ip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), high = COUNT(CASE(cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2 >= 4, 1, null)), passed = COUNT(CASE(event.action == "passed", 1, null)), types = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4), apps = COUNT_DISTINCT(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString1), geo = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Context around the single critical event: many high-rating events and multiple apps = active intrusion; a lone event from an otherwise-quiet internal tester may be a scan artifact.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows the critical exploit with an HTTP 2xx/5xx backend response.
Node.Result: True Positive (Critical Exploit Reached Backend - immediate IR, treat app/DB as compromised)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows action=passed for a critical exploit even without a captured response, from an external source.
Node.Result: True Positive (Critical Exploit Forwarded - escalate, inspect backend)

Node.Condition: INV-02 shows the source is a documented internal scanner and INV-01 shows no backend response.
Single critical event, action=alerted (transparent), internal source, ambiguous ownership.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-F5CRIT-REQUEST, INV-02-F5CRIT-BROADER to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: An approved scanner/tester generating a critical-signature request that did not reach the backend.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the engagement; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: A critical web exploit forwarded by the WAF, potentially compromising the backend.

Indicators.Item: External source or part of a broader attack.

SOCAction.Item: Immediate IR: inspect the target app server and DB for compromise/web-shell.
Block the source; enforce blocking; preserve the full request.
Rotate app/DB credentials if injection reached the DB.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A transparent/staging policy forwarding a genuine critical detection.

SOCAction.Item: Move the policy to blocking immediately; re-triage as TP if backend reach is found.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Inspect the targeted app server/DB now; block the source.
Preserve the full request for forensics.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Enforce blocking; hunt web-shell/persistence; rotate credentials if the DB was reached.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enforce blocking on all public banking policies; virtual-patch the exploited vector.

QualityChecks.Check: Attack-type list matches the critical-class set in the detection.
Single-event fidelity relies on rating>=4 + not-blocked - do not widen without care.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Approved test confirmed; no backend reach; documented.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Backend integrity verified/restored; source blocked; policy enforced; forensics retained.
